description:
## Why

The One Billion Row Challenge (https://github.com/gunnarmorling/1brc) is a text job: a 13 GB file of `<station>;<temperature>\n` lines, 10k distinct station names, output min/mean/max per station. Parsing and aggregating a large text file is exactly the job that sends Elixir developers to Rustler, which makes it a stronger target workload than most numeric ones. It is also the north star for text support in the kernel subset: everything 1BRC needs (bitwise ops, word loads, sub-array views, writable arrays in helper kernels, a hash table over alloc'd arrays, string literals) is what every other byte-level text workload needs too.

## What "text" means in defk

Bytes in, packed arrays or bytes out. A UTF-8 string is a [u8]. No string type, no map type, no Unicode semantics in the subset: Elixir's String module owns graphemes and case. The one rule stays verifiable because every text construct has a byte-level Elixir meaning.

## Shape of the solution

Elixir owns I/O and parallelism: split the file by byte offset, align each chunk to a newline, run one kernel call per chunk under Task.async_stream, merge the small partial tables in Elixir. The kernel owns the hot loop: scan for `;` and `\n`, parse the fixed-point temperature, hash the name, update min/max/sum/count in an open-addressing table held in alloc'd arrays (a [i64] slot array, a [u8] key arena, [i64] stat columns), and return the arrays as a tuple. The runtime contract holds: every call yields.

## Rules (CONTEXT.md, examples/README.md)

- Elixir first: the baseline is the best pure-Elixir solution we can build, marked :optimized before any claim.
- Realistic size declared before measuring: 1B rows / ~13 GB for the verdict; 100M rows (~1.3 GB) is the development size and is reported beside it.
- Comparison with a Rustler port and responsiveness (a /health-style ticker during the run) are reported beside the verdict and never change it.
- Absolute parity with the top Java entries is not the goal; those rely on unsafe memory tricks and all-core tuning the runtime contract forbids.

## Sequencing

```mermaid
graph LR
  base[baseline+generator] --> ex[1BRC kernel example @100M]
  w38[defk-w38 bitwise] --> loads[word loads + wrapping u64]
  w38 --> ex
  loads --> ex
  gqk[defk-gqk arrays via branches] --> slices[sub-array views]
  slices --> ex
  mut[writable array params] --> ex
  lit[string literals] --> ex
  ex --> mmap[mmap-backed input]
  ex --> full[full-size run + verdict]
  rust[Rustler comparison] --> full
  mmap --> full
```

Done when: the full-size run is recorded with a workload verdict against an optimized baseline, and the subset additions it needed are documented in docs/language.md.
title: 1BRC: parse and aggregate a 1-billion-row text file with kernels
